findings.issue:
Nothing bounds the compiled program size of a regular expression. A short repetition such as [a-z]{1000} expands to about 1,000 instructions, and Go accepts about 3.3 million per pattern. Every pattern is compiled three times (the walk, the library, patternCosts), which is unbudgeted O(program) work each time, and the library keeps its copy for the life of the snapshot.

Setup: CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -overlay with probe zz_probe4_test.go (scratchpad r3/), on a quiet 4-vCPU machine, through Factory.Build and Check. Schema {"allOf":[{"pattern":"<[a-z]{1000} repeated R times>x<i>"}, ...]}:
- R=300, 3,328 bytes: Build 0.64 s, 302 MB allocated.
- R=1000, 11,028 bytes: Build 1.56 s, Check 0.96 s, 938 MB allocated, 41 MB kept live.
- R=3000, 33,028 bytes: Build 4.57 s, Check 3.43 s, 2.87 GB allocated, 126 MB kept live.
- Seven R=3000 patterns, 231,130 bytes (within MaxSchemaBytes): Build 25.0 s, Check 19.6 s, 20.1 GB allocated; the built Filter keeps 886 MB live (Sys 2.4 GB).
- Under load: 4,000 properties, each {"pattern":"[a-z]{1000}x<i>"} (153,796 bytes): CompileSchema 3.47 s and 1.7 GB.

This breaks doc.go's own claims: a whole compile under about 0.6 s, at most about 300 MB allocated and 18 MB held at once, and a compiled Schema keeping at most about 9 MB.

Runtime consequence (probe zz_probe9_test.go): schema {"properties":{"code":{"type":"string","pattern":"<[a-z]{1000} x1000>x"}}} at the 10 MiB default. The body {}, which never reaches the pattern, reserves 64,049,408 bytes. Eight concurrent 2-byte requests exhaust the 512 MiB maxBufferedBytes, and every gate then gets 503. With R=100 the charge is 6.4 MB per request.
findings.fix:
1. Add a proposed RZ-CFG-005 rule bounding the program size of each pattern and of all patterns of a document (for example 2^14 instructions per pattern and 2^17 per document). Compute it from the parsed syntax tree, counting repeat multiplicities, before any regexp.Compile in walker.rules, so neither the walk nor the library compiles an oversized pattern. Record it in doc.go and in the req 75 contract request or OQ row.
2. Charge the matcher transient only when a string or member name actually reaches a pattern, for example when the value's dimScan is greater than 0.
3. Add a deterministic test that the largest admitted patterns stay within the bound.
4. Add the case to BenchmarkCompileAnalysisWorstCase, so the doc's compile figures cover it.

findings.issue:
In the location pass, every failing minContains or maxContains error keeps a []int of every item index that matched contains: 8 bytes per item, up to 16 with append's spare capacity. The model charges this nowhere. An item is charged only the units of the contains schema at its kind; for `contains: true`, `{}`, or a type that admits the item, that is 0. So an array of n matching items under L in-place evaluations holds 8*n*L bytes but is charged only 2 units per evaluation. The work bound caps n*L at about 3.4e6 at the default limit, so up to about 27 to 54 MB per request goes unreserved, and the cap grows with the raw limit. This bypasses maxBufferedBytes.

**Library behavior (jsonschema/v6@v6.0.3, validator.go:401-428).** `arrValidate` appends every matching index to `matched []int`. In the location pass, `vd.error` keeps the error kind, so `kind.MaxContains{Got: matched}` and `kind.MinContains{Got: matched}` keep the whole slice in the returned tree. That is 8 bytes per matching item, more with append's spare capacity.

**Model.** working.go:517 counts one unit each for contains and maxContains on an array, and minContains adds nothing. `bodyScan.array` (working.go:932-964) has no term per item for the matched list. Each item is charged only the units of the contains schema at its kind, which is 0 for `true`, `{}`, or a type that admits the item.

**Results.** Schema is an in-place chain of 100 `$ref` links, each with `"contains":true,"maxContains":0`.

The propertyNames charge is wrong in both directions.

(a) Over-charge: a PropertyNames wrapper error is charged for every member name whenever any evaluation applies propertyNames, even when ka.full == 0 (the scan has decided the name cannot fail). Valid map-like objects are refused with 413:
- {"type":"object","propertyNames":{"maxLength":64},"additionalProperties":{"type":"integer"}} with 450,000 members "m000000":1 (5,400,001 B, 51% of 10 MiB): 413 errWorkingSetTooLarge; decide = 86,400,208 = 450,000 x 192 + 208, so every name pays one errorBytes although no error can exist. Without propertyNames the same body passes, reserving 54 MB.
- "propertyNames":{"pattern":"^[a-z0-9_]+$"} with 250,000 members (3.0 MB, 29%): 413, decide 96,000,208.
- Same pattern with 300,000 members "key_000000":"value" and additionalProperties {"type":"string"} (6.3 MB, 60%; decoded cost only 18.9 MB): 413, decide 115,200,104.

(b) Under-charge: only one wrapper is charged per name, but each evaluation that applies propertyNames adds its own wrapper for a failing name. Exact trees (decisionTree, locationTree) on an object of 2,000 members "n00000":1:

- {"anyOf":[{"propertyNames":{"enum":["a","b"]}} x50]}: 1.31x and 1.12x.
- {"allOf":[{"propertyNames":{"type":"integer"}} x200]}: location 102,708,984 against 89,984,192 (1.14x).

findings.evidence:
The code at working.go:1015-1018 (bodyScan.object, propertyNames branch) charges `if ka.evals > 0 { b.locate += errorBytes; keys += (ka.full+1)*errorBytes }`: one wrapper per name, whether or not the name can fail, and never more than one. (a) Over-charge, reproduced:

- The request side's per-request bound becomes raw + 4x + 8x = 13 times maxRequestBodyBytes (130 MiB at the 10 MiB default), which changes the documented 150 MiB per request.
- Measured at the default: valid records pass up to 81% of the limit and line items up to 70%, both limited by jsonval's decoded cost (4.9x and 5.7x, above R-63's 'about 3 times'); strings under a pattern up to 84%; dense one-character enum arrays up to 31%. R-63's 'typical documents fit at the full limit' needs the owner's decision on jsonval cost.

07 req 75 and section 9 item 21:
- Replace 'at most MaxEvaluations at any nesting depth up to 64' with a nesting limit. The first depth at which the root's evaluation count may exceed MaxEvaluations (4,096) is the schema's nesting limit.
- A body value that deep is 413 RZ-RT-003 through filter.ErrTooLarge (proposed).
- A nesting limit below MinNesting (16) is RZ-CFG-005 at the crossing.
- Cite the rich-text schema (limit 28) and the component tree (limit 20) as accepted shapes.

07 req 75, fan-out:
- Define it as the largest product over schema paths that repeat no schema; that is how '$ref cycles counted once' is read.
- It is computed exactly per strongly connected component. Past fanOutSteps (65,536) steps within one component, a sound upper bound decides: the product of each schema's largest factor times the largest fan-out leaving the component.

07 reqs 76 and 80, number bounds (OQ rows):
- Schema side: the bounds apply only to the values the library parses, which are the 5 numeric keywords, the 8 integer keywords and everything inside const and enum.
- Body side: a number is refused (400 DetailNumber) only where the library may parse it: a numeric keyword or the integer type at its own path, a uniqueItems array above it, or a const or enum value holding arrays or objects above it. Where the per-path state is unknown, the document-wide flag (Schema.ComparesNumbers) applies.

07 req 84 and PB 'Per-stage latency budget': BenchmarkValidate1KiB is now about 89 µs, against about 70 µs before. The decision pass's wrapper and the per-path scan (5.6 to 7.9 µs) add the difference; library validation is about 60 µs of the total. The 25 µs p50 target needs an OQ or a decision on the library.

07 req 90 and F6, compile: a worst-case compile takes up to about 0.51 s (BenchmarkCompileAnalysisWorstCase), allocates up to about 305 MB in total, peaks at about 18 MB live, and the compiled Schema keeps up to about 9 MB, of which the states are up to about 5 MB at maxStates and maxTransitions. Ordinary schemas take milliseconds and keep kilobytes.

filter.Factory contract (WP-01 comment 'An error carries an RZ-CFG code') and WP-70: Factory.Build now returns errors from filter.Shared, such as a canceled snapshot compile, unchanged and uncoded, and a foreign shared value as a plain error. The snapshot compiler should treat an uncoded Build error as internal, not as a configuration finding.

make gates or the nightly jobs: run BenchmarkWorkModel and BenchmarkPatternModel on the reference machine and fail when any ns/unit exceeds 1. That is the calibration check the wall-clock unit tests used to make; on this machine at rest the maximum is 0.80.

WP-02 (internal/jsonval): with MapObjects:true, charge decoded values at their real layout. A map[string]any's hash table holds 336 bytes for 1 to 8 members; past that, power-of-two tables of 33 bytes per slot filled to at most 7/8, plus about 160 bytes per table, and about 96 bytes per member past one table of 1,024 slots. Also charge the spare capacity append leaves in []any (exact capacities 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 71, 143, 303, 591, 1023; at most 0.67n up to 4,095 items and 0.31n past) and each string's rounding to its allocation size class. Until then WP-51 adds these bytes in its scan (mapExtra, arrayExtra, stringExtra) and reserves them, but the architecture R-63 413 stop (filter.DecodedLimitFactor times the raw limit) still applies to jsonval's lower charge. Arrays of small objects can therefore decode to about 3.3 times that limit before the 413. Please decide with the spec owner whether R-63's stop should move to the true cost.

Spec owner (07 section 9 item 21, OQ-performance-budgets row (b)): please record the new proposed bounds of WP-51.
- The work bound now also charges the location pass's walk over the error tree: walkWork, 192 + 2 units per byte of the longest error location, per error unit. A failing body whose two passes and walk exceed the work limit, or whose request ends during the walk, gets DetailMismatch alone.
- Compile-time pattern work is bounded per document by steps: patternBudget and regexpBudget for the run-queue exploration, and matchBudget (2^25 work units) for name/pattern matching. Past them the analysis assumes the worst, which never refuses a document.
- The nesting limit is refined: a body value at or past the schema's nesting limit is refused (413) only when its own path's state is unknown or may exceed MaxEvaluations. A free-form member nested deep under a recursive schema now validates.
